claims.text: Polymer programs conferred between 118 and 179 degrees a year from 2014 through 2021, an average of 139, then 54 in 2022 and 63 in 2023, under half that average; the adjacent materials programs held their usual range (pipeline lede, h2 'fallen below half its old pace', the annual trend chart and its table).

claims.text: The region staffs from the floor, pays the top under the nation, and now trains half as many. Akron pays its high-school-majority occupations a median 3% under the national rate and its degree occupations 7% under it, or 0.97x and 0.93x the national medians. The polymer programs behind those degree jobs conferred 63 degrees in 2023, against an average of 139 a year through 2021. Both findings point the same way for an employer here: the occupations the region is known for are the ones it pays furthest under the rate and the ones its universities now confer fewest of; whether that is a shortage or a correction, these files cannot say.
